tasks.body: Implement plan.md Task A. Create src/slugify.mjs exporting slugify(input): return a lowercase slug where every run of characters that is not an ASCII letter or digit becomes a single '-', leading and trailing separators are removed, and an input with no ASCII letters or digits becomes ''. Do not transliterate diacritics; non-ASCII letters count as separators. Create test/slugify.test.mjs using node:test and node:assert/strict, with one assertion per acceptance line: slugify("Hello, World!") === "hello-world"; slugify("  a  --  b  ") === "a-b"; slugify("!!!") === ""; slugify("a_b") === "a-b"; and the input is never mutated (for example, pass a String object or check the original value is unchanged after the call). Add no dependencies. Touch only the two listed files. Run npm test and report its output.

Implement plan.md Task B. Create src/titleCase.mjs exporting titleCase(input): uppercase the first letter of every word and leave every other character exactly as it was; never lowercase anything. A word starts at the beginning of the string or after any character that is not a letter or digit. Create test/titleCase.test.mjs using node:test and node:assert/strict, with one assertion per acceptance line: titleCase("hello world") === "Hello World"; titleCase("iOS device") === "IOS Device"; titleCase("a-b c_d") === "A-B C_D"; titleCase("") === "". Add no dependencies. Touch only the two listed files. Run npm test and report its output.

Implement plan.md Task A. Create src/slugify.mjs exporting slugify(input): return a lowercase slug where every run of characters that is not an ASCII letter or digit becomes a single '-', leading and trailing separators are removed, and an input with no ASCII letters or digits becomes ''. Only ASCII letters (A-Z, a-z) and ASCII digits (0-9) count as letters or digits; do not transliterate diacritics, and treat every non-ASCII character as a separator. Create test/slugify.test.mjs using node:test and node:assert/strict, with one assertion per acceptance line: slugify("Hello, World!") === "hello-world"; slugify("  a  --  b  ") === "a-b"; slugify("!!!") === ""; slugify("a_b") === "a-b"; and the input is never mutated (for example, check the original value is unchanged after the call). Add no dependencies. Touch only the two listed files. When done, run the repository's full test suite with 'npm test' from the repository root (the package.json script, which runs every test/*.test.mjs file, not only test/slugify.test.mjs). The full 'npm test' must pass, and you must report its complete output.

Implement plan.md Task B. Create src/titleCase.mjs exporting titleCase(input): uppercase the first letter of every word and leave every other character exactly as it was; never lowercase anything. Only ASCII letters (A-Z, a-z) count as letters and only ASCII digits (0-9) count as digits for titleCase, the same rule Task A uses for slugify. A word starts at the beginning of the string or after any character that is not an ASCII letter or digit, so every non-ASCII character, including accented letters, acts as a word boundary, and non-ASCII characters are never changed. Create test/titleCase.test.mjs using node:test and node:assert/strict, with one assertion per acceptance line: titleCase("hello world") === "Hello World"; titleCase("iOS device") === "IOS Device"; titleCase("a-b c_d") === "A-B C_D"; titleCase("") === "". Add no dependencies. Touch only the two listed files. When done, run the repository's full test suite with 'npm test' from the repository root (the package.json script, which runs every test/*.test.mjs file, not only test/titleCase.test.mjs). The full 'npm test' must pass, and you must report its complete output.
